'''Robert William Bilger''' {{post-nominals|country=AUS|FAA}} (22 April 1935 – 2 October 2015<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.eoas.info/biogs/P001416b.htm|title=Bilger, Robert William - Biographical entry|last=|first=|date=|website=Encyclopedia of Australian Science|publisher=The University of Melbourne eScholarship Research Centre|language=en-gb|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110811124442/http://www.eoas.info/biogs/P001416b.htm |archive-date=2011-08-11 |access-date=2020-01-31}}</ref>) was a South African born Australian engineer.

Born in Rustenburg, South Africa, on 22 April 1935, Bilger studied both a Bachelor of Engineering in Mechanical Engineering and a Bachelor of Science in Mathematics at [[University of Auckland|Auckland University College]] in New Zealand.<ref name="AAS">{{Cite web|url=https://www.science.org.au/academy-newsletter/australian-academy-science-newsletter-102/obituaries |title=Bob Bilger Obituary |website=Australian Academy of Science  |access-date=2024-03-20}}</ref>

He was awarded a [[Rhodes Scholarship]] in 1956 and, in 1961, received a Doctor of Philosophy in Engineering Science from [[Exeter College, Oxford|Exeter College]], [[University of Oxford]], submitting a dissertation titled "The Behaviour of pitot and static holes in fluid flow" completed under the supervision of Professor A. Thom. <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rhodeshouse.ox.ac.uk/alumni-volunteers/rhodes-scholar-database/ |title=Bob Bilger |website=Rhodes Scholar Database  |access-date=2020-02-09}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://solo.bodleian.ox.ac.uk/discovery/fulldisplay?docid=alma990204331940107026&context=L&vid=44OXF_INST:SOLO&lang=en&search_scope=MyInst_and_CI&adaptor=Local%20Search%20Engine&tab=Everything&query=any,contains,Bilger,AND&mode=advanced&pfilter=rtype,exact,dissertations,AND&offset=0 | title=Thesis Search| website=SOLO Database| access-date=2025-09-18}}</ref> In 1965 he joined the [[University of Sydney]] as a senior lecturer in mechanical engineering before becoming a professor in 1976, where he remained until his retirement in 2006.

He was awarded the status of Fellow in the [[American Physical Society]], after being nominated by the Division of [[Fluid dynamics|Fluid Dynamics]] in 2002, for "outstanding contributions to knowledge of turbulent reactive flows through insightful [[experiment]]s, theory and modelling, especially for elucidating the fundamental processes in turbulent combustion and for the development of the conditional moment closure."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2002&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellows 2002|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=2017-04-20}}</ref>

Bilger was made a Fellow of the [[Australian Academy of Technology and Engineering]] in 1987, and later elected as a Fellow of the [[Australian Academy of Science]] in 2003.<ref name="AAS" /> For outstanding contributions to [[combustion science]], he was awarded the Ya. B. Zeldovich Gold Medal by [[The Combustion Institute]] in 1992.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.combustioninstitute.org/resources/awards/ya-b-zeldovich-gold-medal/|title=Ya. B. Zeldovich Medals|website=www.combustioninstitute.org|language=en|access-date=2023-08-17}}</ref> Due to the impact of his research and his involvement in the organisation of combustion conferences, the primary keynote lecture during the biannual Australian Combustion Symposium is known as the "Bilger Lecture".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.anz-combustioninstitute.org/bilger.php|title=Bilger Lectures|website=www.anz-combustioninstitute.org|language=en|access-date=2023-08-17}}</ref>
